tools.name: get_alerts_object
tools.title: Get alerts object
tools.description:
Retrieve a specific alert definition, alert event, or case by ID.

Use this tool when the user has an alert-related ID but the object type is unclear. The tool can try multiple alert object types automatically, or you can provide a hint.

For a case with 30 or fewer events, the case's full event history is returned (`case_events`, newest-first, including full per-event detail like comment text, actor, and timestamps). For a case with more than 30 events, only a de-duplicated summary of event *types* is returned instead (`case_event_types`, a list of `{event_type, count}`), to bound response size. Use the `get_case_events` tool to fetch full event detail for cases above that threshold, optionally filtered by type and paged - that tool also returns events newest-first.

Args:
    object_id: Alert object ID. Must be a UUID, or a readable case ID like ``CASE-123``.
    object_type_hint: Optional hint for the expected object type: ``alert_definition_by_id``, ``alert_definition_by_version_id``, ``alert_event``, or ``case``.
    get_watch_data: If true, also fetch watch data (query plus triggering records) for the most relevant alert event tied to the object.

Returns:
    JSON string with ``search_id``, ``found_type``, ``found_object``, and optional ``warning`` / ``watch_data``.

tools.name: get_case_events
tools.title: Get case events
tools.description:
Retrieve full case event detail (comment text, actor, timestamps, and other event-specific data) for a case, with optional filtering by event type and paging.

Events are returned newest-first, so with the default offset the most recent activity is on the first page; page further with `offset` to reach older events.

Use when you need to view history of case activity (e.g. when a user was assigned).

Returns:
    JSON string with paging metadata (``total_case_events``, ``filtered_by_event_type_total_count``, ``offset``, ``page_size``, ``has_more``) and the ``events`` list.

tools.name: get_service_catalog_entities_data
tools.title: Get Service Catalog Entities Data
tools.description:
Get column data — RED metrics (latency percentiles, throughput, error rate), health (policy evaluation status), resource saturation (CPU/memory/OOMKilled for k8s-pod; heap/thread/GC for jvm), and dependencies (``dependencyLatencyPerRequest``, ``timeConsumingDependencies``) — for one time window, optionally grouped and filtered. Omit ``entity_id`` to query across every entity of the type, or set it to drill down into exactly one named entity; both return the same response shape.

Args:
    entity_type: An entity type from ``list_service_catalog_entity_types`` (either form, e.g. "service" or "ENTITY_TYPE_SERVICE").
    start: Window start, unix seconds.
    end: Window end, unix seconds (must be > start).
    columns: Column ids to fetch, from the entity type's schema (e.g. ["errorRate", "totalRequests", "health"]).
    entity_id: Optional. Scopes the query to exactly one named entity (e.g. one service), exactly as returned by ``list_service_catalog_entities``. When set, ``limit``/``sort_column``/``sort_order`` are not supported — a single entity has at most one row/series per group.
    group_by: Optional. Labels to group rows by (e.g. ["service_name"]). Capped at the schema's ``group_by_limit``.
    filters: Optional. List of ``{label_name, label_values, metric_label_name?}``; multiple filters combine with AND, ``label_values`` combine with OR.
    data_aggregation_type: "table" (default, one row per group for the whole window) or "timeseries" (one series per group/column, with datapoints over the window).
    limit: Optional. Max rows to return (table aggregation only; not supported with ``entity_id``).
    sort_column: Optional. Column id to sort by (table aggregation only; not supported with ``entity_id``) — use with ``limit`` to find top/bottom offenders (e.g. highest ``errorRate``).
    sort_order: Optional. "asc" or "desc" (table aggregation only; not supported with ``entity_id``).
    widget_name: Optional. Free-form label attached to the query for server-side telemetry/attribution.

Returns:
    For "table": JSON with ``rows`` (one flat dict per group, entity identity fields merged with each requested column's resolved value or ``{"error": ...}``) and ``columns`` (metadata: id/display_name/unit). For "timeseries": JSON with ``series`` (one entry per group/column with ``datapoints``), ``columns``, and ``total_series_count``.

tools.name: get_service_catalog_entity_type_schema

tools.description:
Get the schema for one service-catalog entity type: available data columns (RED metrics, health, resource saturation, dependencies, ...) and the labels it can be grouped or filtered by. Columns and labels differ per entity type (e.g. ``service`` exposes ``errorRate``/``health``/``dependencyLatencyPerRequest``; ``k8s-pod`` exposes ``cpuUtilizationProm``/``k8sPodMemoryWorkingSet``/``oomKilled``; ``jvm`` exposes ``jvmHeapUsedPercent``/``jvmThreadCount``/GC columns).

Args:
    entity_type: An entity type from ``list_service_catalog_entity_types`` (either form, e.g. "service" or "ENTITY_TYPE_SERVICE").

Returns:
    JSON with ``columns`` (id/display_name/unit), ``default_columns``, ``groupable_labels``, ``group_by_limit`` (max labels combinable in one ``group_by``), ``default_group_by``, ``filterable_labels``, and ``required_filters``.

tools.name: get_service_map_relations_graph
tools.title: Get service dependency graph
tools.description:
Get a graph of interactions between services from Coralogix tracing for a specific timeframe.

If ``service_name`` is omitted, the tool returns a compact full service-map graph as an adjacency map.
If ``service_name`` is provided, the tool returns only services interacting with that service, including node and edge details.

Args:
    time_range: Optional time range with ``start_time`` and ``end_time`` in ISO-8601 UTC format.
        If omitted, defaults to the last hour.
    service_name: Optional service name to focus the graph on.

Returns:
    JSON string with ``service_map``. For a focused service query this is a detailed graph with ``nodes`` and ``edges``.
    For an unfiltered query this is a compact adjacency graph keyed by source service.

tools.name: list_infrastructure_filters
tools.title: List Infrastructure Filters
tools.description:
List the attributes infrastructure resources can be filtered by, with their accepted values.

This is the discovery step before filtering in ``list_infrastructure_resources``: attribute names are per resource type and dynamic, so never guess one.

Args:
    category: Optional. Limit to one category, e.g. "Hosts".
    resource_type: Optional. Limit to one resource type within the category.

Both narrow the result and both may be omitted: pinning a type gives that type's attributes, a category alone spans its types, and omitting both gives the union across every type.

Returns:
    JSON array of ``{name, kind, wildcard, values, types}``. ``kind`` is what the value looks like — ``string`` is free text, ``status`` is a fixed set, and ``number``, ``bool`` and ``date`` mean themselves. ``values`` lists the accepted values of a fixed set; pass one of them, spelled as reported. ``wildcard`` says whether a ``*`` is accepted in the value. ``types`` names the category/type pairs carrying the attribute, which is what makes the unpinned form usable.

tools.name: list_infrastructure_resource_types
tools.title: List Infrastructure Resource Types
tools.description:
List the available infrastructure resource types (category/type pairs).

Categories and types are dynamic per account, so never guess them. To learn what resources can be *filtered* by rather than which types exist, use ``list_infrastructure_filters``.

Returns:
    JSON array of ``{category, type, label}``. Pass ``category`` and ``type`` verbatim to ``list_infrastructure_resources`` (as its ``category`` and ``resource_type`` arguments). Some entries may have an empty ``type``; those cannot be listed.

tools.name: list_infrastructure_resources
tools.title: List Infrastructure Resources
tools.description:
List infrastructure resources matching a filter, one page window at a time.

Call ``list_infrastructure_filters`` first whenever the attribute is not already known — it returns the attribute names, which values a fixed set accepts, and where a ``*`` is allowed. Never guess an attribute name or a status value.

At least one of ``category``, ``resource_type`` or ``resource_filter`` must be given; none is required on its own.

Args:
    category: Optional. Resource category, e.g. "Hosts".
    resource_type: Optional. Resource type within the category, e.g. "EC2_Instances".
    resource_filter: Optional. A filter tree. Each node is exactly one of:
        ``{"match": {"field": "<attribute>", "values": ["<value>", ...]}}`` — the values OR each other.
        ``{"bool": {"op": "AND" | "OR", "operands": [<node>, ...]}}`` — nests freely.
        So ``OS=linux AND (Health=Critical OR Region=eu-west-1)`` is
        ``{"bool": {"op": "AND", "operands": [{"match": {"field": "OS", "values": ["linux"]}}, {"bool": {"op": "OR", "operands": [{"match": {"field": "Health", "values": ["Critical"]}}, {"match": {"field": "Region", "values": ["eu-west-1"]}}]}}]}}``.
        A ``*`` in a value is a wildcard, allowed only where ``list_infrastructure_filters`` reports ``wildcard: true``. A status attribute accepts only the values it lists.
        Requiring several values of one attribute means one ``match`` node per value under a ``bool`` ``AND``, which is how to narrow on two substrings at once: ``{"bool": {"op": "AND", "operands": [{"match": {"field": "Name", "values": ["*alert*"]}}, {"match": {"field": "Name", "values": ["*processing*"]}}]}}`` returns the names holding both.
        ``Category`` and ``Type`` are not filterable attributes — they have their own arguments, never appear in ``list_infrastructure_filters`` output, and a ``match`` on them is rejected.
    name_filter: Optional, legacy. Case-insensitive substring match on the resource's display name. Requires ``category`` and ``resource_type``, and cannot be combined with ``resource_filter`` — prefer filtering on the name attribute.
    scope_filter: Optional, legacy. Map of scope key to value; allowed keys are ``service``, ``environment``, ``team``, combining with AND. Requires ``category`` and ``resource_type``, and cannot be combined with ``resource_filter``.
    start_row: Optional. First row of the page window (default 0).
    end_row: Optional. Exclusive end row of the page window (default ``start_row + 100``). The window cannot reach past row 10,000 — narrow the filter instead of paging further.

Returns:
    JSON with ``total_count`` (fleet-wide match count, independent of the window), ``returned_count``, and ``resources`` (array of ``{resource_id, name, category, type, columns}``). Compare ``total_count`` against ``returned_count`` before reasoning over the rows: if it exceeds what you can page to, narrow the filter rather than paging further. Never pages automatically — keep paging while ``start_row + returned_count < total_count``. A valid attribute that is simply unpopulated returns 0 rows; that is an answer, not a failure to retry. Pass ``resource_id`` values verbatim to the health-history and raw-data tools.

tools.name: manage_ai_custom_evaluation
tools.title: Manage custom AI evaluation
tools.description:
Manage **custom evaluation policies** and their links to applications. Pick `action`:
- `create` (needs `body`): create a custom evaluation policy. `body` holds name, instructions, policyType, and optional description/violates/safe/examples/applicationIds.
- `update` (needs `evaluation_id`, `updates`): partial patch of a custom evaluation policy — omitted fields are left unchanged.
- `add_policy` (needs `evaluation_id`, `application_id`): attach a custom evaluation policy to an app.
- `remove_policy` (needs `evaluation_id`, `application_id`): detach a policy from an app. Removes only the link; the policy object survives and can be re-added. (This is how you 'remove' a policy from an app — there is no policy delete.)
Returns JSON.

tools.name: manage_ai_evaluation
tools.title: Manage AI evaluation
tools.description:
Create, update, or delete a **configured evaluation** (a policy enabled on an AI application). Pick `action`:
- `create` (needs `application`, `subsystem`, `config`, `target` [PROMPT|RESPONSE]; optional `is_enabled`, `threshold`): enable an evaluation on an app. `config` is the EvaluationConfig object (the `$case` variant + its fields).
- `update` (needs `evaluation_id`, `updates`): partial patch — include only the fields to change; omitted fields are left unchanged.
- `delete` (needs `evaluation_id`): remove the evaluation from its app. Destructive and not reversible.
Returns JSON.

tools.name: manage_ai_model_pricing
tools.title: Manage AI model pricing
tools.description: Set the team's custom per-model pricing overrides. `action` is `set` (needs `prices`). Pricing is **team-wide** (not per-app) and applies to new data only; `set` replaces the whole set — pass the full map, or an empty map `{}` to clear all overrides. `prices` maps model name to a pricing object {inputPricePerMillionTokens, outputPricePerMillionTokens, cacheReadPricePerMillionTokens, cacheWritePricePerMillionTokens}. Returns JSON.

tools.name: manage_alerts
tools.title: Manage Coralogix Alerts
tools.description:
Unified tool for all Coralogix alert operations.

Actions:
- create: Create a new alert. Requires 'alert'.
  IMPORTANT: Always ask the user for priority (P1-P5) - never pick one yourself.
  Returns: { message, alertId }

- get: Get alert by ID. Requires 'id'.
  Returns: { message, alert }

- list: List alerts. Optional 'nameFilter' for case-insensitive name matching.
  Returns: { message, alerts }

- update: Update existing alert. Requires 'alert' (must include 'id' field).
  IMPORTANT: First use get/list to fetch the existing alert, modify it, then pass the complete alert here.
  Returns: { message, alertId }

- delete: Delete alert by ID. Requires 'id'.
  IMPORTANT: If you only have the alert name, use list with nameFilter first to find the ID.
  Returns: { message }

- generate_openapi: Generate OpenAPI JSON payload. Requires 'alert'.
  IMPORTANT: For existing alerts, use get/list first to fetch it.
  Returns: { message, openAPIDefinition }

- generate_kubernetes: Generate K8s YAML for Coralogix Operator. Requires 'alert'.
  IMPORTANT: For existing alerts, use get/list first to fetch it.
  Returns: { message, k8sYAML }

- generate_terraform: Generate Terraform HCL for Coralogix Provider. Requires 'alert'.
  IMPORTANT: For existing alerts, use get/list first to fetch it.
  Returns: { message, tfHCL }

Required fields by action:
- action: Always required
- id: Required for get, delete
- alert: Required for create, update, generate_openapi, generate_kubernetes, generate_terraform
- nameFilter: Optional for list

tools.name: manage_alerts_scheduler
tools.title: Manage Coralogix Alerts Schedulers
tools.description:
Unified tool for all Coralogix alerts scheduler operations.

Actions:
- create: Create a new alerts scheduler. Requires 'alertsScheduler'.
  Returns: { message, alertsSchedulerId }

- get: Get alerts scheduler by ID. Requires 'id'.
  Returns: { message, alertsScheduler }

- list: List alerts schedulers. Optional 'nameFilter' for case-insensitive name matching.
  Returns: { message, alertsSchedulers }

- update: Update existing alerts scheduler. Requires 'alertsScheduler' (must include 'id' field).
  IMPORTANT: First use get/list to fetch the existing alerts scheduler, modify it, then pass the complete alertsScheduler here.
  Returns: { message, alertsSchedulerId }

- delete: Delete alerts scheduler by ID. Requires 'id'.
  IMPORTANT: If you only have the alerts scheduler name, use list with nameFilter first to find the ID.
  Returns: { message }

- generate_openapi: Generate OpenAPI JSON payload. Requires 'alertsScheduler'.
  IMPORTANT: For existing alerts schedulers, use get/list first to fetch it.
  Returns: { message, openAPIDefinition }

- generate_kubernetes: Generate Kubernetes YAML for Coralogix Operator kind AlertScheduler. Requires 'alertsScheduler'.
  IMPORTANT: For existing alerts schedulers, use get/list first to fetch it. Alert-ID filters generate deterministic placeholder Alert resource refs.
  Returns: { message, k8sYAML }

- generate_terraform: Generate Terraform HCL for coralogix_alerts_scheduler. Requires 'alertsScheduler'.
  IMPORTANT: For existing alerts schedulers, use get/list first to fetch it.
  Returns: { message, tfHCL }

Supported subset:
- exactly one of filter.metaLabels or filter.alertsUniqueIds
- all-alert filters are rejected because the current operator AlertScheduler CRD requires exactly one alert selector
- one-time schedules, recurring always-active schedules, and recurring dynamic daily, weekly, and monthly schedules

Required fields by action:
- action: Always required
- id: Required for get, delete
- alertsScheduler: Required for create, update, generate_openapi, generate_kubernetes, generate_terraform
- nameFilter: Optional for list

tools.name: manage_dashboards
tools.title: Manage Coralogix Dashboards
tools.description:
Unified tool for Coralogix Custom Dashboard operations.

This tool follows the Management API. generate_terraform reports shapes the
Terraform provider cannot express, such as an unattached action or a
goToDashboardId. Supported widget types: markdown, lineChart, dataTable, gauge,
pieChart, barChart, horizontalBarChart, hexagon, dynamic.

Every widget except markdown takes a query with exactly one source: logs,
metrics, spans or dataprime. The query shape follows the widget:
- lineChart carries groupBy, groupBys and aggregations on the query. dataTable
  carries the same under query.<source>.grouping, because the API models it so.
- pieChart, barChart and horizontalBarChart take one aggregation plus groupNames
  and optional stacking.
- gauge and hexagon reduce the result to one number per group. Only a gauge
  takes query.logs.aggregation and query.spans.aggregation.
- dynamic is different: it takes queryDefinitions, a list, and then one
  visualization form that draws them. Use describe_schema with dynamic to see
  the fifteen forms and their fields.

A widget can carry actions, the links offered on it. A dashboard can carry
variablesV2, variables, filters, annotations and unattachedActions above its
widgets. All are omitted here; fetch each with describe_schema and its name.

IMPORTANT: To change an existing dashboard, first use get (or list to find the
ID) to fetch the dashboard, modify the returned document, then pass the complete
document to update. Dashboards are replaced whole, not patched.

IMPORTANT: create, update, get, and generate_* use MCP JSON in 'dashboard'.
validate uses API-language JSON. Before create: generate_openapi, then
validate with that openAPIDefinition, then create with the original MCP
dashboard. issue.location is an API JSON Pointer.

Actions:
- create: Create a new dashboard. Requires 'dashboard' in MCP JSON. Any 'dashboard.id' is ignored so the server assigns a new one.
  Returns: { message, dashboardId }

- get: Get a dashboard by ID. Requires 'id'.
  Returns: { message, dashboard, accessPolicy }

- list: List dashboards from the dashboard catalog. Optional 'nameFilter' for case-insensitive name matching.
  Returns: { message, dashboards }

- update: Replace an existing dashboard. Requires 'dashboard' with 'id'.
  Returns: { message, dashboardId }

- delete: Delete a dashboard by ID. Requires 'id'.
  IMPORTANT: If you only have the dashboard name, use list with nameFilter first to find the ID.
  Returns: { message }

- generate_openapi: Generate the OpenAPI JSON create payload. Requires 'dashboard' in MCP JSON.
  The dashboard ID and the server-generated slug are removed, so the payload creates a copy.
  Returns: { message, openAPIDefinition } which is API-language JSON for validate.

- validate: Check without saving. Requires API-language JSON in
  'openAPIDefinition', or 'id' for a saved dashboard. Do not pass MCP JSON in
  'dashboard'. Pass a JSON object. A JSON string is also accepted for backward
  compatibility. Empty issues means valid. Issues are not a tool error.
  Returns: { message, issues }

- generate_kubernetes: Generate Kubernetes YAML for Coralogix Operator kind Dashboard. Requires 'dashboard'.
  Returns: { message, k8sYAML }

- generate_terraform: Generate Terraform HCL for coralogix_dashboard. Requires 'dashboard'.
  Returns: { message, tfHCL }

- describe_schema: Get the full JSON Schema for one omitted part. Requires 'schemaName', whose description lists the available names; omit it to get the lists.
  IMPORTANT: The input schema is the dashboard skeleton only. Widget bodies,
  the dynamic widget's visualization forms, a widget's actions list and the
  dashboard-level lists are left as bare objects. Call describe_schema with a
  name before building one.
  Returns: { message, schemaName, schema }
  or, with no schemaName, { message, schemaNames, dynamicForms, dashboardLists, widgetLists }

Required fields by action:
- action: Always required
- schemaName: Optional for describe_schema
- id: Required for get, delete. For validate, checks a saved dashboard; mutually exclusive with openAPIDefinition
- dashboard: Required for create, update, generate_*. MCP JSON. Rejected by validate
- dashboard.id: Required for update
- openAPIDefinition: Required for validate unless id is set. API-language JSON object. A JSON string from generate_openapi is also accepted for backward compatibility
- nameFilter: Optional for list
- accessPolicy: Optional for create, update, and generate_*

tools.name: manage_quota_allocation_rule_set
tools.title: Manage Coralogix Quota Allocation Rule Set
tools.description:
Unified tool for the Coralogix team quota allocation rule set.

Quota allocation splits the team's daily ingest quota across telemetry types such as logs, spans, and metrics. There is one set per team. The API has no list and no resource id path.

Get the live set, change the full customer rule list, then create or update to replace that list. Update is not a patch of one rule. Delete clears customer-managed rules only. After delete, get still succeeds. Coralogix-managed rules (cxManaged true) may remain. get returns those rows so you can see them. create, update, and generate_openapi omit them and never send cxManaged.

Known entityType values include logs, spans, metrics, cpuProfiles, memoryProfiles, browserLogs, browserLogs/v2, sessionRecordings, olly, auditEvents, alerts, quotaEvents, engineQueries, engineSchemaFields, labsLimitViolations, notificationDeliveries. entityType is a free string.

Actions:
- create: Replace all customer rules using POST. Requires 'quotaAllocationRuleSet' with the full customer 'rules' list. Send rules: [] to clear customer rules. Omitting rules is invalid.
  Returns: { message, quotaAllocationRuleSet }

- get: Get the live team set. Do not send an id.
  Returns: { message, quotaAllocationRuleSet }

- update: Replace all customer rules using PUT. Requires 'quotaAllocationRuleSet' with the full customer 'rules' list.
  IMPORTANT: First use get, modify the complete customer list, then pass the complete quotaAllocationRuleSet here. Do not send only the rules you changed.
  Returns: { message, quotaAllocationRuleSet }

- delete: Clear customer-managed rules. Do not send an id. get still works afterward.
  Returns: { message }

- generate_openapi: Generate the write OpenAPI JSON body (no cxManaged). Requires 'quotaAllocationRuleSet'.
  Returns: { message, openAPIDefinition }

- generate_kubernetes: Generate Kubernetes YAML for Coralogix Operator kind QuotaAllocationRuleSet. Requires 'quotaAllocationRuleSet'.
  Returns: { message, k8sYAML }

- generate_terraform: Generate Terraform HCL for coralogix_quota_allocation_rule_set. Requires 'quotaAllocationRuleSet'. Always includes the rules attribute, including rules = [].
  Returns: { message, tfHCL }

list is not supported. This team has one rule set. Use get.

Required fields by action:
- action: Always required
- quotaAllocationRuleSet: Required for create, update, generate_openapi, generate_kubernetes, generate_terraform

tools.name: manage_tco_log_policies
tools.title: Manage Coralogix TCO Log Policies
tools.description:
Unified tool for Coralogix TCO log policy operations.

TCO log policy Terraform and Kubernetes resources are atomic overwrite resources: generated Terraform or Kubernetes describes the complete logs policy list and applying it replaces the complete backend logs policy set. Prefer tcoLogPolicies for generation. Single-policy generation is allowed but returns a warning.

Priority and dataset routing: a policy sets its priority either at the policy level or on every entry of targets, never both, and one of the two is required. Use targets to route matched logs to specific named datasets, each with its own required priority and optional quota-based priorityOverride and archive retention. Targets must be unique by dataspace and dataset. Omit priority when targets is set. get and list return whichever of the two the policy actually uses, so their output can be edited and fed straight back into update or generate_*.

Matching: a policy matches either by structured rules (severities, applications, subsystems) or by a raw dpxlExpression, never both - when dpxlExpression is set, omit severities, applications, and subsystems. dpxlExpression must start with a version tag such as <v1>. An optional policy-level priorityOverride sets quota-based usage tiers and is only valid alongside a policy-level priority (not with targets, which carry their own per-target priorityOverride).

Actions:
- create: Create a TCO log policy. Requires tcoLogPolicy.
- get: Get a TCO log policy by ID. Requires id.
- list: List TCO log policies. Optional nameFilter performs case-insensitive substring matching by policy name.
- update: Update a TCO log policy. Requires tcoLogPolicy with id.
- delete: Delete a TCO log policy by ID. Requires id.
- generate_openapi: Generate AtomicOverwriteLogPoliciesRequest JSON. Requires tcoLogPolicies or tcoLogPolicy.
- generate_kubernetes: Generate TCOLogsPolicies YAML. Requires tcoLogPolicies or tcoLogPolicy.
- generate_terraform: Generate coralogix_tco_policies_logs HCL. Requires tcoLogPolicies or tcoLogPolicy.

tools.name: manage_tco_rum_policies
tools.title: Manage Coralogix TCO RUM Policies
tools.description:
Unified tool for Coralogix TCO RUM policy operations.

TCO RUM policy Terraform and Kubernetes resources are atomic overwrite resources: generated Terraform or Kubernetes describes the complete RUM policy list and applying it replaces the complete backend RUM policy set. Prefer tcoRumPolicies for generation. Single-policy generation is allowed but returns a warning.

RUM policies mirror log policies but have no dataset routing (no targets), so priority is always set at the policy level and is required. A policy matches either by structured rules (severities, applications, subsystems) or by a raw dpxlExpression, never both: when dpxlExpression is set, omit severities, applications, and subsystems. dpxlExpression must start with a version tag such as <v1> and is evaluated against the canonical $d.* schema (do not reference $d.cx_rum.*). An optional policy-level priorityOverride sets quota-based usage tiers; each tier's priority must be higher than the policy priority (a tier at or below the base has no effect). RUM policies require the RUM policies feature to be enabled for the team.

Actions:
- create: Create a TCO RUM policy. Requires tcoRumPolicy.
- get: Get a TCO RUM policy by ID. Requires id.
- list: List TCO RUM policies. Optional nameFilter performs case-insensitive substring matching by policy name.
- update: Update a TCO RUM policy. Requires tcoRumPolicy with id.
- delete: Delete a TCO RUM policy by ID. Requires id.
- generate_openapi: Generate AtomicOverwriteRumPoliciesRequest JSON. Requires tcoRumPolicies or tcoRumPolicy.
- generate_kubernetes: Generate TCORumPolicies YAML. Requires tcoRumPolicies or tcoRumPolicy.
- generate_terraform: Generate coralogix_tco_policies_rum HCL. Requires tcoRumPolicies or tcoRumPolicy.

tools.name: manage_tco_trace_policies

TCO trace policy Terraform and Kubernetes resources are atomic overwrite resources: generated Terraform or Kubernetes describes the complete traces policy list and applying it replaces the complete backend traces policy set. Prefer tcoTracePolicies for generation. Single-policy generation is allowed but returns a warning.

Traces have no dataset routing (no targets), so priority is always set at the policy level. A policy matches either by structured rules (applications, subsystems, actions, services, tags) or by a raw dpxlExpression, never both - when dpxlExpression is set, omit the structured rules. dpxlExpression must start with a version tag such as <v1>. An optional policy-level priorityOverride sets quota-based usage tiers; each tier's priority must be more restrictive than the base priority (a tier at or below the base has no effect).

Actions:

tools.name: olly_ask

tools.description:
Send a question to Olly AI assistant and get a response.

Args:
    message: The question or request for Olly.
    chat_id: Optional. Pass a ``chat_id`` from a previous response to continue the conversation with context.
    model: Optional. AI model for ``model_choice``. If omitted, the Olly API uses its default.
    should_block: Optional. Default: ``false`` (async). Keep the default for investigations and any non-trivial request: the interaction starts without waiting for completion, returning immediately with ``status=in_progress`` and no ``response`` text - poll with ``olly_get_interaction`` until status is terminal (``completed``, ``error``, or ``stopped``). Only pass ``true`` for a short, simple question you expect Olly to answer almost immediately (for example "what alerts fired today"), where waiting synchronously is simpler than polling.
    agent_to_agent_mode: Optional. When ``true`` (default), Olly acts as a sub-agent to the calling agent: shorter responses, no charts/tables, asks clarifying questions instead of guessing, and relies on the parent agent's broader context.

Returns:
    Async (default): JSON with ``chat_id``, ``interaction_id``, ``status`` (typically ``in_progress``), and a ``note`` to poll via ``olly_get_interaction``.
    Blocking (short questions only): JSON with ``chat_id``, ``interaction_id``, ``status``, ``response`` (assistant text or user-facing fallbacks when empty), and optionally ``interaction_mode`` / ``model_choice``.

    start_date: Range start, ISO 8601 UTC (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`). Default: 15 minutes before `end_date`, or 15 minutes before now if `end_date` is omitted.
    end_date: Range end, ISO 8601 UTC. Default: 15 minutes after `start_date`, or now if `start_date` is omitted.

tools.name: query_promql_instant
tools.title: Run PromQL instant query (metrics)
tools.description:
Run an instant PromQL expression against Coralogix Metrics (Prometheus `query` endpoint).


Args:
    query (str):
        A valid PromQL expression evaluated at a single point in time.
        Example: sum by (service) (rate(http_requests_total[5m])).

    time (str, optional):
        Optional RFC-3339 timestamp (UTC) for the evaluation time.
        If omitted, the query is evaluated at the current time.

Returns:
    Formatted query results (result type, series count, and sample values).
    Large results are truncated with guidance to narrow the query.
    Optional ``warnings`` / ``infos`` from the metrics API are appended when present.

tools.name: query_promql_range
tools.title: Run PromQL range query (metrics)
tools.description:
Run a range PromQL expression against Coralogix Metrics (Prometheus `query_range` endpoint).


Args:
    query (str):
        A valid PromQL range expression (evaluated at each step across the window).
        Example: rate(http_requests_total[5m]).

    start (str):
        RFC-3339 timestamp (UTC) for the start of the time range. Required.

    end (str):
        RFC-3339 timestamp (UTC) for the end of the time range. Required.

    step (str):
        Query step width as duration. Examples: 30s, 20m, 6h, 1d. Required.

        Important note:
        The step size should be large enough so that a series returns ~20 records.
        For example:
        * If the range is 1 hour, the step should be about 3 minutes
        * If the range is 1 day, the step should be about 1 hour
        * For 1 week, about 8 hours, etc.

    limit (int):
        Maximum number of ``[timestamp, value]`` samples kept per series in the tool output (also sent as the API ``limit`` parameter). Must be between 1 and 200. If the API returns more samples for a series, the tool truncates ``values`` and adds truncation fields (see Returns).

Returns:
    JSON string: array of Prometheus ``query_range`` matrix series (the API ``data.result`` list). Each element has ``metric`` (string-to-string label map) and ``values``: an array of ``[timestamp, value]`` pairs. Timestamps and values are often **strings** in Prometheus JSON; Coralogix may return the timestamp as a **number** (Unix seconds) and the value as a **string**. If a series has more than ``limit`` samples, ``values`` is shortened to the first ``limit`` entries and the series gains ``truncated_result`` (bool), ``truncated_result_len`` (same as ``limit``), and ``original_result_len`` (count before truncation).

tools.name: read_rum_sdk_docs
tools.title: Read Coralogix RUM SDK documentation
tools.description:
Get the official Coralogix RUM SDK setup guide and API reference. This is the authoritative source for RUM SDK integration.

**IMPORTANT**: Always use this tool FIRST when the user asks about any of the following — do NOT search the codebase or guess the setup:
- Setting up, installing, or configuring Coralogix RUM SDKs (Browser, React Native, Flutter, Android, iOS)
- Adding RUM monitoring, real user monitoring, or browser/mobile tracking to an app
- Enabling session recording or replay
- Uploading source maps for minified stack traces (@coralogix/rum-cli)
- Understanding minified/obfuscated error stack traces
- Any question about Coralogix RUM SDK configuration options, API, or initialization

Args:
    topic: The documentation topic to fetch. Must be one of:
        - "BROWSER_SDK" - Browser SDK (@coralogix/browser) setup, installation, configuration, initialization, and session recording docs
        - "SOURCE_MAPS" - Source map upload CLI tool docs for de-obfuscating stack traces
        - "REACT_NATIVE_SDK" - React Native plugin (@coralogix/react-native-plugin) setup and configuration docs
        - "FLUTTER_SDK" - Flutter plugin (cx_flutter_plugin) setup and configuration docs
        - "ANDROID_SDK" - Android SDK setup and configuration docs
        - "IOS_SDK" - iOS SDK setup and configuration docs

Returns:
    Plain text extracted from official SDK README or documentation for the selected topic (content may be truncated to a maximum length).

tools.name: search_alert_definitions
tools.title: Search alert definitions
tools.description:
Search alert definitions in the team with flexible filters.

This tool returns up to 30 matching alert definitions. Use the filters to narrow the result set before truncation.

Args:
    order_bys: Optional list of order-by fields.
    name_matcher: How to match `name` values. Default: ``EQUALS``.
    name: Optional list of alert names to filter by.
    alert_type_matcher: How to match `alert_types`. Default: ``EQUALS``.
    alert_types: Optional list of alert types to filter by.
    priority_matcher: How to match `priorities`. Default: ``EQUALS``.
    priorities: Optional list of alert priorities to filter by.
    enabled: Optional filter for enabled/disabled alerts.
    modified_start_time: Optional start time for modification date filtering.
    modified_end_time: Optional end time for modification date filtering.
    last_triggered_start_time: Optional start time for last-triggered filtering.
    last_triggered_end_time: Optional end time for last-triggered filtering.

Returns:
    JSON string of the returned alert definition summary payload.

tools.name: search_dashboard
tools.title: Search indexed dashboards by meaning or ID
tools.description:
Find dashboards by semantic search or retrieve one's indexed summary by ID. For the full definition, use ``manage_dashboards(action="get")``.

Exactly one of ``query`` or ``id`` must be provided:
- ``query`` performs semantic search across indexed dashboards.
- ``id`` fetches one dashboard's indexed summary, which may be incomplete.

Args:
    query: Natural-language description of the dashboard to find. Mutually exclusive with ``id``.
    id: Exact Coralogix dashboard ID. Mutually exclusive with ``query``.
    limit: Maximum search results when using ``query`` (1-100, default 10). Ignored when ``id`` is provided.

Returns:
    When ``query``: JSON string with ``total`` and ``results``.
    When ``id``: JSON string with the indexed dashboard summary. Large dashboards may include ``truncated`` metadata.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.title: Search Coralogix docs
tools.description:
Search official Coralogix docs by title or path.

Args:
    query: Search text (for example "MCP setup" or "API keys").
    limit: Max results (1-20, default 5).

Returns:
    Plain-text list of matching doc titles and path suffixes (under /docs/).

tools.name: search_for_fields
tools.title: Search log/span fields by description and/or example value
tools.description:
Batch search for log or span DataPrime field paths by description and/or value. Supports up to 5 search items at once.

Each search item should be one of:
- {"description": "..."} - Search by semantic description (e.g., "customer identifier fields")
- {"value": "..."} - Search by entity/value (e.g., "Acme Corp", "production"); case-insensitive substring match on schema-store example values.

Args:
    search_items: List of search items (up to 5). Each item is either a description or value search (not both).
    source: Dataset to search: ``logs`` or ``spans``.

Returns:
    Search results with matching field paths and descriptions.

tools.name: search_labels
tools.title: Search label names across metrics
tools.description:
Find label names matching a substring across all metrics. Use when the user mentions a dimension/filter but you don't yet know which metric carries it, then follow up with `search_relevant_metrics(<label>, mode="by_label")`. See the metrics skill for the full workflow.

Args:
    substring: Substring to match against label names (case-insensitive), e.g. "user_email" or "email".

Returns:
    One matching label name per line (exact match first), or an error if none match.

tools.name: search_queries
tools.title: Search saved dashboard queries
tools.description:
Search saved dashboard queries by meaning or by field reference.

Use ``search_type`` to choose the mode:
- ``semantic``: semantic search over saved dashboard queries. Requires ``query_text``.
- ``by_field``: find saved queries that reference a specific field path. Requires ``field_path``.

Args:
    search_type: ``semantic`` or ``by_field``.
    query_text: Natural-language query description for semantic search.
    field_path: Exact field path for field-based lookup, such as ``metadata.service``.
    limit: Maximum number of results to return (1-100, default 10).

Returns:
    JSON string with ``total`` and ``results``.

tools.name: search_relevant_metrics
tools.title: Search relevant metrics
tools.description:
Discover metrics by description, name pattern, or label. See the metrics skill for the full workflow.

Args:
    query: The search term, interpreted per `mode`.
    mode:
        - "by_description" (default): semantic search over a natural-language description of what to measure.
        - "by_name": wildcard metric-name pattern, e.g. "http_*", "*_total".
        - "by_label": list the metrics exposing an EXACT label name, to pick a bridge metric for a PromQL join (use after `search_labels`).
    top_k: Max results, by_description only (default: 5).
    name_filter: by_label only — metric-name substring to narrow a truncated result.
    join_key_label: by_label only — an EXACT second label (the shared join key); returns only metrics carrying BOTH labels on the same series.

tools.name: show_dataprime_command_details
tools.title: Show DataPrime command syntax and details
tools.description:
Show details for a specific DataPrime command or function.

Args:
    kind: Which section of the catalog to include: ``all`` (commands and functions), ``commands`` only, or ``functions`` only.
    name: The exact name of the command or function to show details for.

Returns:
    JSON string with ``count`` and ``items``. Each item has ``name``, ``type`` (``command`` or ``function``), ``syntax``, ``description``, and ``category`` (``description`` may be shortened in the payload).
